text:
ravi: Noticed a weird divergence on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate in us-west after today's rollout. p95 up ~20ms, p99 up ~130ms. p50 flat. Only affects small requests (<30 tokens).
jordyn: same spike. The "merged" line that shows all-variants moved; individual variant traces point to rdw-gpt-q4-fastbatch.
marta: timeline: rollout canary increased from 5% -> 40% at 08:20. infra-bot: deploy: canary-rollout-2026-03-23T08:20 -> 40% confirmed.
kevin: quick hypothesis: our percentiles on dashboards are computed from merged tdigest sketches. If merge doesn't account for per-variant sample counts, the smaller sketch with extreme tail will pull blended p99.
ravi: i ran a quick export of raw samples for the hour: ```curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'https://telemetry.internal/api/raw?from=6174442000&to=6174445800&route=/v1/generate&env=us-west' | jq .lat_ms```
jordyn: raw counts for window: q4-fastbatch=310, q3-stable=5400. If merge is unweighted that explains the jump.
telemetry-bot: rollup-metadata: {"merged_sketches":true, "merged_count":null} (emitted at 08:30).
kevin: ugh. we should be emitting merged_count and using a weighted merge algorithm. I'll open a telemetry PR to 1) emit merged_count, 2) change merge to weighted by count, 3) add unit tests for unequal counts.
marta: console-ux - can we show provenance on the latency panel (raw vs merged, and merged=weighted/unweighted) and display sample counts in the legend?
console-ux: yes. will add a provenance pill and count badge on hover. quick patch target: tomorrow morning.
ravi: operationally, two parallel issues: (A) possible merge bias in telemetry; (B) batching kernel wait behavior in fallback/pool spillover causing real tail for small payloads. we need to triage both.
kevin: logging notes: i also saw worker_queue_depth for fallback pool spike to 9 at the same time. infra-bot: fallback-us pool average queue depth 9.1 between 08:22-08:28; pool count 5 workers.
jordyn: that queue depth with batched kernels could add waiting latency: if kernel waits X ms for batch fill that's added to small requests.
marta: suggested short-term mitigations: 1) split the dashboard default to show per-routing-policy (strict vs spillover) to prevent surprising blended metrics; 2) reduce canary weight to 5% until telemetry fix lands; 3) scale fallback pool by +2 workers.
kevin: i prefer scale-up + reduce weight if needed. i'll trigger scale and coordinate rollback if queues don't drop.
ravi: i'll annotate the dashboard with the canary timeline and add a one-line note "blended percentiles may be influenced by merged sketches; check raw samples if p99 changes unexpectedly."
console-ux: also adding a temporary tooltip that warns when merged sketches are unweighted (we can detect merged_count==null).
kevin: opened PR #812: "tdigest: weighted merge + emit merged_count". cc @jordyn for tests.
jordyn: reviewing. test plan includes simulated sketches with counts 100 vs 10 and assert blended p99 matches weighted raw sample merge.
marta: filed INC-1252: "p99 spike on latency dashboard during canary - possible tdigest merge bias + fallback queueing". paging @sre-oncall.
telemetry-bot: INC-1252 created (severity: p2).
ravi: final: we'll do quick telemetry fix + dashboard provenance, scale fallback pool, and step down canary to 5% if the queue persists. Postmortem to capture the multi-factor root cause (merge artifact vs real queueing).
